question.question:
D2 — Which TTHW target should this quickstart journey be held to?
Project/branch/task: main branch, PLAN.md SDK quickstart docs, DX POLISH mode.
ELI10: TTHW (time to hello world) is the clock from a developer reading step 1 to their first SDK call returning something they understand. For your persona the declared 8-step journey is ESTIMATED at 25-60 minutes of hands-on work, plus an UNKNOWN wait for an emailed API key. Peers report 2-5 min (Stripe) and 3-20 min (Twilio) from self-serve signup, but their clock excludes running a local server and has no human gate, so the minutes are not directly comparable. The target you pick sets the bar every later score is measured against; it does not approve any specific fix.
Stakes if we pick wrong: too ambitious and the review demands changes DX POLISH cannot deliver; too lenient and the review blesses a journey the rubric calls Red Flag (>10 min, 50-70% abandon).
Recommendation: B because the rubric's Competitive tier is where peers sit, and it names the gap honestly without pre-committing to a hosted sandbox or new service.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=8/10, C=3/10, D=n/a
Pros / cons:
A) Champion (< 2 min)
  ✅ Matches the best-in-class bar the rubric ties to 3-4x adoption
  ✅ Forces every step of the current journey to justify itself
  ❌ Feasibility: not reachable while the key is email-gated and a local Postgres is required; would push beyond DX POLISH scope
B) Competitive (2-5 min) (recommended)
  ✅ Peer-level bar; makes the gap to today's ESTIMATED 25-60 min explicit in every pass
  ✅ Leaves remedies open: each fix is still its own decision later
  ❌ Blocker: the email key gate alone likely exceeds this window; hitting it needs at least one process change you have not yet approved
C) Current trajectory (~25-60 min + key wait)
  ✅ No pressure on scope; review documents the journey as-is
  ✅ Honest about what exists today
  ❌ Rubric classifies this as Red Flag (>10 min); scores will read as failing against no target for improvement
D) Tell me what's realistic
  ✅ You know the team's constraints (key policy, infra) that I cannot see
  ✅ Sets a bar the team will actually own
  ❌ Requires you to name a number now
Net: trading an honest peer-level bar (with a known email-gate blocker) against either an unreachable bar or no bar at all.

Reported peer figures (Stripe, Twilio) land in the 3-5 minute band, but against a hosted API with a self-serve key and a canned endpoint, so the numbers are not directly comparable. The skill's tiers: >10 min is the Red Flag band (reported 50-70% abandonment).

Recommendation: D because no target in A-C is honest under both the declared facts and the POLISH scope. I propose a split clock: active time target of 5-10 min (Needs Work tier, reachable via docs polish) while the key wait is measured separately and reported as an unresolved blocker, with hosted-sandbox/self-serve-key listed as out-of-scope opportunities.

B) Competitive (2-5 min)
